sources.entry: INGInious - Intelligent grader that allows secured and automated testing of code made by students. (Source Code, Clients) AGPL-3.0 Python/Docker

summary.one_liner: INGInious is a Python intelligent grader that runs students' code inside Docker containers for secured, automated testing and grading.
summary.what_it_does: INGInious provides a backend that manages interaction with Docker and grades submitted code, plus a frontend where students submit code through a web interface. The frontend also has an administration interface that lets teachers track student progress and edit exercises. The README says it can be used as an external grader for Moodle or edX. Installation is described via docker compose, with a superadmin account configured through environment variables, including password (argon2id-encoded), username, language and indentation. The frontend is exposed through the Caddy reverse proxy, using a sample config at deploy/Caddyfile. Courses are added by placing task folders in a tasks directory, and manual pip installation is also mentioned.
use_cases: running untrusted student code in a sandbox
external grader for Moodle or edX
tracking student progress in a coding course
hosting programming exercises for a university course
how_to_run: Open the browser and log in with the default superadmin / superadmin credentials (set INGINIOUS_SUPERADMIN_PASSWORD in docker-compose.yml for production)
Optionally add 127.0.0.1 inginious.local to /etc/hosts and use that address
git clone the demo-tasks repository and move the tutorial folder into the tasks directory to add a course
notable: Runs student code inside Docker containers to isolate it from the host
Includes a teacher administration interface for progress tracking and editing exercises
Can serve as an external grader for Moodle or edX
Superadmin account and settings configurable through environment variables; UI available in several languages
Course content is added by dropping task folders into a tasks directory
caveats: The README advises that untrusted code should not be run unless SELinux is enabled for the Docker containers
Production deployments must change the session secret key and API secret key in the sample configuration
Default superadmin credentials are insecure and must be changed
Possible permission errors on the tasks directory when it is created by docker compose
